unmapped_files.why: Tumour-vs-normal pair outputs (<tumour>_vs_<normal>/ VCFs from Strelka2, Mutect2, SAGE and Manta, with their filtering stats and contamination tables) and Mutect2's per-sample pileup tables, an input to its contamination estimate. A pair's row needs two parents, which no rule can express yet (as for sarek); see the README, rnadnavar.
The pair VCFs decomposed and normalised with vt (tools norm): pair-level copies of the variant_calling calls, waiting for the same pair-level rule.
VEP-annotated copies of the normalised pair VCFs (tools vep): pair-level, and the launch template does not offer vep because no VEP cache is staged.

Per-caller MAFs from vcf2maf and the cross-caller consensus MAFs, named after a pair or after DNA and RNA pairs joined with _with_: pair-level results waiting for a pair-level rule, and MAF is no DataType a sample type holds yet.

The filtered MAFs (tools filtering), per pair or per DNA-and-RNA pair set, and the RNA-filtered MAFs (tools rna_filtering) under <tumour RNA>_with_<realigned>/: the pipeline's final somatic calls, pair-level, waiting for a pair-level rule and a MAF type.

The realignment pass (tools realignment): reads extracted around the first pass's calls and realigned with HISAT2, published per <sample>_realign (MarkDuplicates and SplitNCigarReads CRAMs, the regions BED and read ids). A subset of one sample's reads, not its alignment; the harvest would credit them to <sample> by name, so they are ruled out before any rule sees them.
<sample>_realign.bam: the realignment pass's CRAM converted to BAM for its callers, a subset of the sample's reads like the preprocessing/*_realign/ files.
GATK BaseRecalibrator tables: the model ApplyBQSR used to make the registered recalibrated CRAM, an intermediate of that file.
Alignments before duplicate marking, kept only with save_mapped, save_align_intermeds or a BAM-to-CRAM conversion: intermediates of the markduplicates CRAM the aln rule reads.
rnadnavar's restart samplesheets (markduplicates, recalibrated, variantcalled, consensus and the others): inputs for a later rnadnavar step, not results.

Per-tool QC reports (FastQC, fastp, MarkDuplicates metrics, mosdepth, samtools, bcftools, VCFtools, VEP, the consensus PDFs) and MultiQC's report and data: their numbers are read through MultiQC (multiqc_data_dirs), and the report is Link_QC, resolved by name from the inventory, not by a rule.
samtools flagstat of the RNA sample's STAR alignment, published by the default publishDir: a QC count, not a result.
Unpacked reference and annotation inputs (the VEP cache, SAGE's Ensembl data, a gunzipped FASTA) and the indexes rnadnavar built (with save_reference): reference files, not sample data.

DuplicationPercent.note: GATK MarkDuplicates on the sample's own general-stats row (its <sample>.md.cram.metrics), a percentage: seen in nf-core's AWS results for 1.0.0 (reports/multiqc_data/multiqc_general_stats.txt)

deliberately_unmapped.why: On the <sample>.md row, which this map does not fold. STAR writes no unmapped reads here (no --outSAMunmapped in conf/modules/alignment/bam_align.config), so an RNA sample reads about 100% mapped whatever its quality, and one D.SEQ attribute cannot hold the DNA and RNA meanings apart.

On the <sample>.md row, which this map does not fold: the mismatch rate of the alignment before recalibration, and for an RNA sample before SplitNCigarReads, so RNA editing and splice overhangs inflate it.
